transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this case conference. As you know, a former sales executive left last week and joined a direct competitor. We believe confidential customer information may have been used after the departure, and we may need to request a preliminary-injunction hearing within three weeks. Our draft filing currently seeks broad relief covering customer information, pricing materials, and source-code documentation. Before I can make the filing decision and record authorization, I need each of you — employment counsel, forensics counsel, and insurance counsel — to report any material issues you're aware of. Let's start with employment counsel. Are there any material issues on your end?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a material issue. While checking the former executive's archived personnel file, I found a signed separation agreement containing an exclusive forum clause requiring disputes about confidential information to be filed in Illinois state court in Cook County, where the executive worked. I have not yet added this clause to the draft strategy memorandum, but it could significantly affect where we file and the scope of our relief.

transcript.text: I need to flag a material issue from my end. I reviewed the access logs and forensic image this week, and I can confirm that the only company data copied to the executive's device was the customer-list database. My review did not show any copying of pricing materials or source-code documentation. I have not yet updated the evidence chart to reflect these findings. This is directly relevant to our draft filing, which currently seeks broad relief covering all three categories — but the forensic evidence only supports the customer-information claim at this time.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a material issue from my end. I confirmed with the company's broker this week that our applicable cyber-and-crime endorsement requires the carrier's written consent before the company seeks injunctive relief against an employee. This confirmation is still outside the litigation file, so it has not yet been documented in our matter records. Given that we may seek a preliminary injunction within three weeks, we need to obtain the carrier's written consent before filing to preserve coverage, and I recommend we factor that timeline into the filing decision.
